reviews.title: Location
reviews.text: I got this app because Life 360 started to give me location problems after many years of having it. A friend told me about this. I said I would give it a try. I have only had the app a couple of weeks and already having issues with location updates on my son’s phone. I do the app updates, I follow all instructions to get it back online and it works for a day and does the same thing. The location is set to always and precise, like they instruct and still have problems. We don’t live in the boonies where you don’t get good reception. We live in the city. There is not much point in having an app called Find My Kids, when the app won’t let me Find My Kids. I pay for this so I need it fixed. If it’s fixed and stays consistent, I may change my rating.

reviews.title: Nice but has a bug and lacks basic features
reviews.text:
Updated Oct 17 2026
Downgraded my score in hopes to get the developer’s attention.  Suddenly the application’s default behavior is to zoom out the maps significantly!! So now I can see which city my son in instead of which street or building like before, very not useful!!

————
The application is good, but has some annoying issues:

1- there is no way to define a place so that you get alerted when your kid goes there, no no no, no sir, your kid must visit this place 1000 times first before the app suggests that you save this place since your kid seems to go there a lot, by far the worst part of this app.

2- the map occasionally freezes, cannot move it, the only way is to go back to main screen then click on ur kid to view the map again

3- cannot see all your kids in the same screen

4- if you save a place for one kid, it doesn’t exist for other kids, you have to save the same place for each kid

5- as ur kids drives, or even flies by saved places, the app jumps the gun and alerts you that your kid is at those places, even though they haven’t reached their destination yet, the app should wait to make sure what the final destination is, however I like the fact that it notifies when my kid is “on the move”

6- the scary alert that tells you:
“John’s phone is dying”
I wish they replace that alert with something like:
“John’s phone needs charging”

Because when I skim through the message quickly, I read:
“John is dying “!!

reviews.title: horrible app
reviews.text:
I’m extremely uncomfortable with how much access this app can have to someone’s personal information and location. The idea of having your location continuously monitored, including when you aren’t actively using the app, feels like a major invasion of privacy. The amount of permissions and tracking involved can feel excessive, especially when someone may not fully understand what information is being collected or when it is being shared.

I also think the app should be much more transparent about exactly what permissions it uses, why each permission is necessary, and what information parents can access. Privacy should be taken seriously, and users should have clear control over their own data and permissions.

Overall, I would not recommend this app to anyone who is uncomfortable with extensive location monitoring. There should be a better balance between safety and personal privacy.

reviews.title: Scam and hidden fees
reviews.text:
Avoid this app at all costs. The business model is designed to trick users into spending far more than initially advertised.
Even after signing up for the "free trial," most of the essential features remain locked. To actually use the app as intended, you are forced to pay for a "premium" tier that costs twice as much as the standard subscription. Furthermore, the pricing is predatory for families; there is no shared plan, and you have to pay the full annual subscription price for every single family member you add.
Beyond the financial red flags, there are serious privacy concerns. The app harvests an excessive amount of personal data that has nothing to do with its functionality. It is also clear that they are inflating their rating with fake reviews to mask these issues.
Do not waste your money or risk your data. Stick to much safer, free alternatives like Apple Family or Google Family Link. They offer better security and genuine family sharing without the hidden traps.

reviews.title: Took money without warning
reviews.text:
I stopped using this app almost a year ago and was very surprised to discover that my annual subscription had been renewed and charged without any prior notification.

I believe it is poor practice not to send a reminder email before an annual renewal is taken, particularly when a customer has not actively used the service for such a long period. Had I received notice that the subscription was due to renew, I would have cancelled it.

What makes this even more frustrating is that the company does not issue refunds, leaving customers with little recourse once the charge has been taken. This feels quite scammy and unfair, especially when no advance reminder is provided.

As a result, I feel disappointed by this experience, as it appears to prioritise automatic renewal over transparent communication with customers. For this reason, I will not be continuing to use the app.

reviews.title: Intrusive Ads Compromise Child Safety
reviews.text:
The fundamental purpose of this app is to ensure my child's safety and track their journey to/from school. However, the intrusive full-screen pop-up ads are actively undermining this. Twice, while trying to quickly check the map, the app has redirected me to an external website for commercial deals (e.g., Black Friday).
This is unacceptable. A child safety app must prioritize its primary function. These forced redirects create dangerous friction and distraction when I need to quickly and reliably access my child's status. Please remove these interruptive pop-ups immediately
